dedupe_keys.name: pulse eu prospective upscaling of life cycle scenarios and environmental impacts for eu buildings

description: PULSE-EU is an open-source, archetype-based model that projects the building stock of each of the 27 EU member states from 2020 to 2050, including new construction, maintenance, renovation, replacement and demolition, and computes life cycle greenhouse gas emissions by combining building life cycle assessment from the MMG and SLiCE models with material flow analysis; it extends the Austrian PULSE-AT model. It integrates 15,026 residential and non-residential archetypes with hierarchical inventories built from datasets such as AmBIENCe, Hotmaps and the Building Stock Observatory. In a Nature Communications article of May 2026 by Alaux and co-authors it was used to run 4,096 scenarios, finding that meeting EU targets needs about 8.53 billion tonnes of CO2-equivalent avoided over 2020 to 2050 and that relying mainly on efficiency and cleaner materials would exceed national capacities. The code is run by initialising the data parsers and then a scheduler over commitment files. Coverage: EU27. Access: free code on GitHub and Zenodo (v1.0.0, April 2026); archetype data are on the KU Leuven Research Data Repository under CC BY 4.0. Licence: TU Graz software licence agreement. Caveats: results depend on archetype representativeness and assumed national capacities. Simulation uses: embodied and operational carbon scenarios for EU building stocks. Related records: Invert/EE-Lab and GBDB CarbEnMats.
